newsitem.title: USA: Johnson & Johnson swaps drug brands with Pharmacia.
newsitem.headline: Johnson & Johnson swaps drug brands with Pharmacia.

text.p: Pharmacia & Upjohn and Johnson & Johnson said Thursday they agreed to swap several brands of over-the-counter drugs in a deal designed to reinforce the market positions of both pharmaceutical firms.
The deal did not involve financial terms, said a spokesman for Pharmacia, based in Kalamazoo, Mich.

Pharmacia's U.S. Consumer Healthcare unit said it acquired Nasalcrom, a nasal spray for allergic rhinitis, and PediaCare, a line of children's cough and cold products, from J&J's McNeil Consumer Products unit. It also took over Micatin, an anti-fungal application for athlete's foot, from J&J Consumer Products.
In exchange, New Brunswick, N.J.-based J&J said it acquired Motrin IB pain reliever and Mycitracin, an antibiotic ointment, from Pharmacia.

"This trade is an outstanding opportunity to expand and strengthen our portfolio," said Michael Valentino, president of Pharmacia Consumer Healthcare U.S. "It makes sense for both parties, with each benefiting from strong brand heritage."

Brian Perkins, president of J&J's McNeil unit, said, "The acquisition strengthens McNeil's leadership position in the pain reliever category, providing the company with an excellent platform for accelerated growth."
J&J's stock rose 62.5 cents to $60, while Pharmacia was unchanged at $34.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
